overview: White plays 2.Bd3, a modest development that blocks the d-pawn and does nothing about e5. Black has easy equality with 2...Nf6 or 2...d5 and a free central game. White usually follows with Nf3, c3 or Ne2 and a slow build-up; there is no attack and no theory to speak of.

white_ideas.idea: Develop the bishop to d3 and keep a compact set-up with Nf3, c3, O-O
Hold e4 and wait for Black to commit

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...d5 or ...Nf6 and develop freely
Use the blocked d-pawn: White cannot easily play d4

typical_structures.structure: Open e-pawn game where White has a passive bishop on d3 and a delayed d2-d4

character.notes: Quiet, nothing forcing for either side; Black can equalise by simple development.

soundness.notes: Playable but passive; Black can take the initiative with ...d5 or ...Nf6, so it is mildly inferior rather than dubious.

structure.notes: Tension in the e4/e5 centre with the d-pawn held back by Bd3; undecided, so flexible.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom choose 2.Bd3; it is a pure oddity.

level.notes: No theory and clear ideas, but it asks nothing of the player and gains nothing, so not a first-repertoire pick.

character.reason: Quiet development with no forcing lines, but not especially hard to break down.

soundness.reason: Passive but not losing; Black has no refutation to force.

structure.reason: The e-pawns face each other and White has not yet decided on d4 or d3.

approach.reason: Hardly ever chosen by strong players.

level.reason: Easy to play but not a recommended choice, so not beginner.
